correctness.rationale: The proof follows directly from the affine incentive form. The logit transform makes each coordinate velocity independent of its own logit, giving zero divergence. At the mixed equilibrium the Jacobian is a weighted cyclic shift, so its N-th power is the scalar product of weights times the identity and the characteristic polynomial is exact. Root-angle counting gives the stated unstable dimensions. The two-player odd-parity first integral has an exact zero derivative and coercive strictly convex level sets, proving a nonlinear center. Pure robust equilibria are strict, and their replicator Jacobian is diagonal with negative entries. No finite experiment is used as an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Targeted semantic and web searches for unidirectional binary cycles, replicator dynamics, logit-volume preservation, weighted cyclic Jacobians, inverter parity, and the center case found no source stating or implying the combined theorem. The motivating full text contains no replicator dynamics. The strongest nearby literature establishes conservation/recurrence under zero-sum or antisymmetric assumptions, whereas the present divergence identity uses only unidirectional payoff dependence and therefore applies without a zero-sum hypothesis. The two-player center itself is classical and is explicitly excluded from the novelty claim; originality rests on the complete source-specific volume/spectrum/parity classification and sharp dimension boundary.

value.rationale: The source uses stability/attractor language around a static equilibrium taxonomy but does not specify a learning flow. The theorem supplies a canonical dynamical interpretation and exposes a sharp structural boundary: all mixed equilibria are unstable except the two-player odd-parity center, while even-parity pure equilibria are sinks. The zero-divergence identity additionally shows that this directed-dependency class is logit-volume preserving without a zero-sum assumption. This is a motivated structural result about equilibrium selection, not an arbitrary parameter slice or routine recomputation.
